claims.text: The initial magnetic high-entropy alloy has an FCC structure.
Incorporating Pd increases the alloy's lattice parameter.
The coercivity-enhancing effect should hold in a single-phase crystalline alloy.
The coercivity-enhancing effect is conditional on Pd increasing the lattice parameter.
An increased lattice parameter leads to more homogeneous magnetic properties.
More homogeneous magnetic properties increase the coercive field.
Pd incorporation will increase the coercive field relative to an alloy without Pd.
Formation of intermetallic compounds or additional phases can alter the magnetic properties.
Formation of intermetallic compounds or additional phases may limit the coercivity effect of Pd incorporation.
The relationship among Pd incorporation, lattice expansion, and coercivity may depend on alloy composition.
The relationship among Pd incorporation, lattice expansion, and magnetic response may depend on processing conditions.
The exact relationship among Pd incorporation, lattice expansion, and coercive-field enhancement is not well understood.

contradictions.description: The effect is stated to apply only when Pd increases the lattice parameter, yet failure of Pd to increase the lattice parameter is itself declared falsifying. Under the stated condition, that result instead means the prerequisite was not met and does not test whether lattice expansion increases coercivity.
